long.title: 6 Bugs in Your Brain That Cost You Money
long.promise: Six well-studied mistakes your brain makes with money, each played by a different bug bean with its own study and a one-line patch; the sixth bug has a bug of its own.
long.visual: The Debugger Bean files a bug report on each bean (NEW, FILED, WON'T FIX); sunk-cost bean glued to a seat, anchor bean, envelope bean, a Present vs Future tug of war, a sofa bean, a worried loss bean.
chapters: Bug 6: Loss Aversion (the bug with a bug)
sources_to_check: Kahneman and Tversky (lost ticket vs lost cash)
Gal and Rucker 2018 and replies (loss aversion debate)
long.fact_note: Behavioural economics has replication problems: use only these six, say 'roughly' for the anchoring numbers, do not quote the 37%/86% or Save More Tomorrow figures until verified, leave out Ariely studies, ego depletion and priming. Loss aversion is contested: present both sides.
why: Abstract and useful: the viewer learns six named mistakes and a patch for each, and can repeat them to a friend.
Open lane: the best direct result for 'money mistakes your brain makes' is a 78-minute lecture; 'sunk cost explained' tops out at 718k with nothing polished or animated.
Adjacent demand is big: 12 Cognitive Biases (2.8M), SciShow Psych on restaurants (1.7M), TED-Ed irrational decisions (2.4M).
Beans make it funny and drawable: every bug is a bean; the running gag is the bug-report stamp.

inspired_by.title: 12 Cognitive Biases Explained / How Restaurants Use Psychology to Make You Spend More Money

long.title: 7 Mosquito Hacks, Tested Against the Science
long.promise: Seven popular ways to stop mosquito bites, each checked against a real study, ranked from no effect to partly works; then the three boring things that actually do.
long.visual: Kit the blue bean tries every hack while Moz the mosquito holds up a score card; each hack gets its own gag prop.
chapters: 1-7. Garlic, vitamin B, ultrasonic apps, wristbands, bug zappers, mosquito plants, citronella candles
What actually works: repellent, a fan, tipping out water
reuse_shorts: Could 1 Million Mosquitoes Drain All Your Blood?
sources_to_check: De Obaldia et al., Cell 2022 (why some people attract mosquitoes)
Shelomi 2022, Bulletin of Entomological Research (vitamin B1)
long.fact_note: Verify the fan, wristband and CDC duration figures in the primary sources. Do NOT quote the 74/75/70% fan numbers: that experiment pushed air through a DEET screen. Candle results range from about 14% to 42% depending on the study.
why: Demand next door: TED-Ed's 'why mosquitoes bite some people more' has 2.2M views; MinuteEarth's mosquito-magnet video is 8.1x its channel median.
A real gap: the best result for 'mosquito repellent myths science' has 54k views and the median result 471.
It is a practical, funny myth test: seven hacks, one verdict each, and what to do instead.
It reuses Moz and the mosquito Short.

inspired_by.title: Why Are Some People Mosquito Magnets? / Why mosquitoes bite some people more than others
